chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you were to perform wudu and make the wiping of the two feet a washing, then you intended that that is what is obligatory, it would not be a valid wudu.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with the wiping upon the two feet; and if it becomes apparent to you that you washed, so you washed, then wipe after it, so that the last of what is obligatory is the wiping.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform the wiping of the feet in wudu to ensure it is valid according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of wiping (masḥ) on the feet depends on the specific intention (niyyah) to perform wiping rather than washing, distinguishing it from the Sunni practice of full washing. It establishes that if one washes the feet but intends to wipe, the wiping must be the final act to fulfill the obligatory requirement, highlighting the importance of aligning physical action with ritual intent in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the distinct interpretation of 'wiping' in Quran 5:6 as a partial action rather than a complete washing.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from is father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘Heasws said: ‘If you were to perform Ablution (Wudhu), and make the wiping of the two feet as a washing, then you think that, that is what is necessitated, the would not happen to be an Ablution (Wudhu)’. Then heasws said: ‘Begin with the wiping upon the two feet, and if it is inevitable for you to wash, so wash, and wipe after it, in order for that to be the last of the necessities’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said

the following: “He (the Imam) has said, ‘If you take Wudu’ and instead of wiping your feet wash them, thinking that this is what is obligatory, it is not considered Wudu’.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘First you must wipe your feet. Then if you like to wash them and you did so thereafter wipe them to make it the last obligatory act (of Wudu’).”’
